thread:
maria.h: Heads-up — Cloud KMS audit picked up a burst of decrypts from a service account tied to a short-lived job at 10:04 UTC. Not blocked yet.
jonathan.s: on it. which key and which svc acct?
maria.h: key: projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/app/cryptoKeys/primary. svc: svc-data-worker@redwood-prod.
security-oncall: Received alert from monitor. Initial surge ~10:04-10:09 UTC, ~240 decrypt ops. No more after 10:10.
sre-bot: alert: kms.decrypt_rate_spike (severity: warning) — threshold 50/min, observed 80/min — triggered 2026-02-28T10:07:12Z.
jonathan.s: can we confirm whether those decrypts map to legitimate job runs or a runaway retry loop?
emma.p: I pulled the compute logs for svc-data-worker. There's a spike of retries against our feature extraction job after an upstream datastore timeout. Entries show repeated fetch+decrypt attempts.
maria.h: logging snippet (sanitized): ```2026-02-28T10:04:05Z svc-data-worker request_id=abc123 action=fetch_encrypted_blob kms_key=primary decrypt_status=OK duration_ms=12``` ```2026-02-28T10:05:12Z svc-data-worker request_id=abc124 action=fetch_encrypted_blob kms_key=primary decrypt_status=OK duration_ms=11``` repeated ~240 entries.
security-oncall: good to see decrypt_status=OK. That suggests legitimate key use. Still need to rule out credential compromise or permission sprawl.
jonathan.s: I checked IAM bindings: svc-data-worker has roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on that key and it's scoped from a deploy last week. Only that SA and one test SA in staging have the role. No new IAM changes in the past 30 days in audit logs.
emma.p: timeline: job deployed 2026-02-27T22:40 UTC, first run fine, then upstream DB had a transient 504 at 10:03 which caused retry backoff to misbehave.
security-oncall: containment plan: 1) rotate the short-lived key encryption key (KEK) on the customer-sensitive key? 2) add short-term constraint: set conditional IAM to restrict decryption to known compute region? 3) throttle the worker retries. Thoughts?
maria.h: rotating the key will cause a huge blast radius; downstream objects encrypted under primary would need rewrap. Not ideal mid-incident. Prefer limiting IAM + immediate revoking of the service account token if compromise suspected.
jonathan.s: I propose: (A) disable external network egress from that worker pool for 1 hour, (B) apply a temporary IAM condition requiring requestor service account tag = "data-worker-v2", (C) patch retry logic.
ciso: we need an exec note ASAP describing risk, impact, and customer exposure: estimated affected customer count = 0 (no external access), keys used for internal model metadata only. Also include timeline and mitigations.
emma.p: customer exposure looks nil — decrypts are on internal metadata blobs, not customer PII. Confirmed with data classification.
legal: confirm — if no customer data, we can avoid external notification. We still need to document in compliance logs and SOC report.
security-oncall: action items assigned: maria.h -> draft exec note & incident entry; jonathan.s -> implement IAM condition and throttle; emma.p -> confirm dataset classification and attach proof; support-lead -> standby in case customers inquire.
maria.h: Drafting exec blurb now. Quick version for execs: "We observed an elevated KMS decrypt rate from an internal service account due to a misbehaving retry loop triggered by an upstream timeout. No evidence of credential compromise or customer data exposure. We applied IAM constraints and deployed a retry fix; next steps: audit IAM tokens, add alerting for retry spikes, and add text to SOC record."
jonathan.s: I'll push the IAM Cond policy in 5–10m: ```gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding primary --member=serviceAccount:svc-data-worker@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter --condition="expression=request.auth.claims.tags[0]=='data-worker-v2',title='temporary-constraint',description='limit to v2 pool'"```
security-oncall: please paste the exact command when you run it and post results here. Also capture the existing policy before change.
jonathan.s: saved previous policy to /var/tmp/primary_kms_policy_prechange.json and applied condition. Policy apply returned 200.
emma.p: retry fix deployed to canary at 10:30 UTC, no further spike on canary. Full rollout starting now.
maria.h: exec note ready — pinging @ciso for review, will attach audit snippets.
ciso: reviewed. small edits for tone, added SLA impact note (none). Approve for internal exec distribution.
maria.h: also drafting a short internal advisory for infra/product teams, and a one-paragraph customer-facing FAQ in case support gets a question. Will share for sign-off.
legal: approve internal advisory language. For customer FAQ, include "no customer data exposed" + guidance to contact support if they see anomalies.
support-lead: ready to publish a canned response if needed.
security-oncall: post-incident tasks: 1) add retry-spike detector to KMS metrics, 2) automate IAM policy snapshot weekly, 3) run token audit for svc-data-worker and rotate creds if any stale tokens found. Assigning owners in incident doc.
maria.h: creating incident record in the tracker and will link to this thread. Thanks all.
jonathan.s: closing loop — IAM condition worked, canary rollout successful, full rollout completed at 10:52 UTC. No ongoing decrypt activity.
security-oncall: marking incident status: resolved -> monitoring. Will keep monitoring 24h.
maria.h: final note: we avoided key rotation to prevent rewrap work; saved in postmortem options list for longer-term key design improvements.
jonathan.s: tl;dr: false alarm (bug), fixed, no customer impact, actions for durable prevention. :white_check_mark:
